newsitem.title: UK: Sugar freight market calmer towards end week.
newsitem.headline: Sugar freight market calmer towards end week.

text.p: Business was calmer on the sugar freight market on Thursday as Brazil again provided a focus for demand and shipments started to trickle out of Europe with the onset of the region's sugar beet harvest, shipbrokers said.
Jean Lion issued a revised order for 12/13,000 tonnes of bagged sugar from Continent to Dammam or Dubai for prompt shipment dates.
Andre quoted for 14,000 tonnes of bagged sugar from south Brazil to the Mediterranean, again for prompt dates.
Shipbrokers said the only posisble firm business came from Sofracom and Brazilian shippers SIMAB.

Sofracom was said to have fixed 12,000 tonnes in bulk on its usual run from Reunion to Marseilles and SIMAB 14,000 tonnes in bags from north Brazil to the Red Sea with option of the Egyptian Mediterranean for prompt dates.
Details of the rates have yet to emerge for both orders.
Elsewhere, Libya postponed the deadline for bids in its white sugar buying tender until Friday with replies scheduled for Monday.
Libya tendered to buy 14,000 tonnes of white sugar for shipment in November/December.
